newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean police fire teargas to disperse students.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean police fire teargas to disperse students.

text.p: South Korean riot police entered a Seoul campus on Sunday and fired teargas to try to disperse about 1,000 students holding a protest rally over a controversial new labour law, witnesses said.
They said armour-plated police vehicles fired volleys of teargas at the students, who initially fled but then regrouped and started hurling rocks at the police.
Witnesses said police first sprayed small quantities of teargas at the students to prevent them marching out of the Hanyang University campus.
The campus lies about five km (three miles) from Myongdong Cathedral, where seven trade union leaders are sheltering from arrest.
Groups of workers and students have clashed regularly with riot police in the streets of Seoul since the government rammed the labour bill through parliament on December 26.

The government still has arrest warrants out for unionists at Myongdong, even though they have backed away from a call for all-out stoppages. They have said they would limit industrial action over the law, which allows companies to sack workers.
